A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Raw-JPEG Adapter work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete supplementary materials support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original compression, cross-camera generalization, ablation and image-rendering experiments, including supplementary results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds bitrate-controlled results and an ISP-rendering comparison.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same network, channel-wise lookup tables, pixel-wise gamma mapping, optional DCT scaling, inverse operations and training losses. The added rate-control procedure is an evaluation protocol, not a revised adapter.

E1.justification: v3 adds a limited qualitative rendering scenario involving an iPhone 15 ISP alongside simplified and S24 rendering pipelines (Figure 6). Quantitative compression and rendering coverage remains S24, S7, MIT-Adobe FiveK, NUS and Kodak; the new bitrate experiment uses S24.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same comparators, including OLM, raw-to-sRGB mapping, fixed gamma, CIE XYZ Net, Invertible ISP, INF and R2LCM. The new bitrate experiment uses the existing direct-JPEG comparator. Revised Invertible ISP scores do not change comparator membership.

E3.justification: v3 retains fixed-quality evaluations and adds approximately matched-bitrate testing at targets of 0.50, 0.75, 1.00 and 1.25 BPP (Appendix B.2). Per-image binary search selects JPEG quality, uses the nearest trained adapter model and counts COM metadata toward total storage. This adds a substantial control over the storage-fidelity comparison.

E4.justification: The new bitrate-control analysis tests whether fidelity gains persist under comparable storage budgets. Figure 6 adds a qualitative case study of simplified versus complex ISP rendering. Existing component, loss and parameter-size ablations are unchanged, including v1 Table 7, now v3 Table 8.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty estimates. Reported averages remain image-level aggregate results.

E6.justification: Table 4 changes Invertible ISP PSNR from 24.76 to 43.71 dB, SSIM from 52.98 to 98.40 and MS-SSIM from 84.15 to 99.56, with similarity metrics scaled by 100. This substantially changes its comparative standing. New v3 Table 7 reports bitrate-controlled results, including 40.44 versus 38.55 dB for the DCT adapter and JPEG at 0.50 achieved BPP. Other matched tables retain their numerical results.

T1.justification: Equations 1–21 retain the same formulation, operator constraints, DCT derivation, JPEG simulation and weighted-BPP definition. No theoretical assumptions, proofs or mathematical definitions are added or revised.

C1.justification: The central claims of lightweight invertible preprocessing, improved raw fidelity, cross-camera generalization, codec compatibility and post-capture editing remain unchanged. The matched-bitrate experiment supplies additional support for the existing compression-fidelity claim.

C2.justification: v3 explains how JPEG-compressed inputs and complex local ISP processing make its reconstruction comparisons harder than prior evaluations using uncompressed, simply rendered inputs (Appendix A.4). Section 2.2 also clarifies the role of operator coefficients versus reconstruction metadata. Existing limitations concerning artifacts, storage overhead and camera-specific DCT behavior remain.

D1.justification: v3 newly documents baseline training and input provenance, including R2LCM training on paired S24 raw and JPEG-rendered images and INF fitting at test time. Appendix B.2 specifies rate search, model selection and metadata accounting. These disclosures do not establish that the retained experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: v3 adds Karaimer and Brown's software camera-pipeline reference and expands discussion distinguishing its operator metadata and evaluation conditions from earlier raw-reconstruction work. The broader related-work categories and research positioning remain intact.

P1.justification: Section 2.2 and parts of the results and discussion are rewritten or expanded, and new evaluation-protocol and fixed-bitrate subsections are added. Supplements are relabeled A/B and references move behind the supplementary text. Most existing prose and the main section sequence remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column formatting, extensively resizing and relocating figures and tables. v1's radar chart and artifact example are merged into v3 Figure 5; a new ISP comparison becomes Figure 6 and a bitrate table becomes Table 7. Supplementary displays are also redistributed, including among reference pages.

improvement.justification: The matched-bitrate experiment addresses storage-rate confounding in v1's fixed-quality comparisons, while the added baseline-protocol explanations improve interpretability. The gain is limited: rate matching is approximate and compares only against direct JPEG, and the substantial Invertible ISP score revision remains unexplained. The method and most existing evidence are unchanged.
